summary: This benchmark evaluates whether a frozen attention router trained purely on register keys and write orders can transfer address-selection capability to an independent model with a disjoint value vocabulary. Through controlled baselines and counterfactual value swaps, the study demonstrates payload-independent address transfer (85-88% accuracy vs <0.3% shifted sham), while transparently reporting that the transferred router provides no accuracy advantage over native end-to-end training.
strengths: Rigorous experimental design incorporating multiple negative controls, including cyclically shifted attention scores and frozen untrained routers.
Careful causal verification using counterfactual interventions on gold and stale writes to confirm that position scores drive value retrieval independently of payload content.
Transparent and honest reporting of negative findings, including missed pre-registered thresholds and lack of superiority over native local training.
Clear reporting of statistical confidence intervals resampled across whole programs.
weaknesses: Evaluated exclusively on a small synthetic register-routing toy task rather than full-scale transformer language models or established natural language benchmarks.
Exploration is limited to two training seeds and a single routing parameterization without exploring varying context depths or multi-head dynamics.
The transferred router fails to outperform native training on longer programs, limiting immediate practical utility for fine-tuning pipelines.
suggestions: Scale the benchmark to standard multi-query associative recall (MQAR) or needle-in-a-haystack tasks within pre-trained open-weight transformer layers.
Evaluate whether transferring routing distributions across heterogeneous model dimensions or architectures yields computational speedups during fine-tuning.
Formally register the supporting repository in the submission metadata rather than relying on inline commit links.

claims.text: Pointer Networks (arXiv:1506.03134) use neural attention as a pointer to select discrete elements from an input sequence.
Dynamic Neural Turing Machines (arXiv:1607.00036) implement a trainable memory addressing scheme maintaining separate content and address vectors.
Zoology (arXiv:2312.04927) formalizes associative recall benchmarks to evaluate parameter-efficient recall capabilities across attention and gated-convolution models.
Cyclically shifting the graft's position scores dropped task accuracy to 0.18% and 0.30% across the two test seeds.
claims.source: Internal experimental reporting and audit data table (Seed 101/503 and Seed 211/607)

novelty_vs_existing.title: Pointer Networks
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: While Pointer Networks generate pointers to input tokens for variable-length combinatorial tasks, this submission isolates whether a learned pointer distribution can be transplanted across independent models with completely disjoint value vocabularies.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Dynamic Neural Turing Machine with Soft and Hard Addressing Schemes
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: D-NTMs train separate address and content representations end-to-end within a single controller; this benchmark specifically tests zero-shot modular transfer of addressing weights between independently trained donor and recipient networks.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Zoology: Measuring and Improving Recall in Efficient Language Models
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Zoology measures associative recall across model families, whereas this benchmark directly tests the causal modularity of position routing weights under key and request counterfactual perturbations.
